suggestions: Convert metadata inventory into individual OSCE files: Each OSCE should be separate file with actual imaging content (not placeholder paths)
For radiology OSCEs, include actual image findings: E.g., CARD-OSCE-0012 (Bradycardia) should describe ECG findings (HR 42, sinus rhythm, PR 280ms, Mobitz I pattern), not just 'ECG for assessment'
Apply systematic interpretation frameworks: CXR → ABCDE, ECG → 7-step (rate/rhythm/axis/intervals/P/QRS/ST-T), CT head → ABC (asymmetry/blood/CSF spaces)
Add technical quality assessment: For CXR → rotation (clavicular heads equidistant?), inspiration (6 anterior ribs?), penetration (vertebrae visible behind heart?)

Include differential diagnoses: E.g., GENE-OSCE-0028 (Lung Cancer) → 'Right upper lobe mass 4.5cm, spiculated margins, hilar lymphadenopathy. DDx: 1) Primary lung cancer (likely), 2) Metastasis, 3) TB (less likely given appearance)'

Add management implications: E.g., CARD-OSCE-0019 (Silent MI) → 'Pathological Q waves V1-V4, ST depression I/aVL → Old anterior MI. Immediate: Aspirin, cardiology consult, troponin, echo to assess LV function'
Use Australian terminology: 'Pulmonary oedema' (not edema), 'Theatre' (not OR), 'Paracetamol' (not acetaminophen), 'Adrenaline' (not epinephrine)

Separate radiology OSCEs from non-radiology: Endoscopy (GENE-OSCE-0020, GAST-OSCE-0033,0038), blood tests (GENE-OSCE-0024,0025), clinical assessments (GAST-OSCE-0045) → delegate to clinical documentation expert
Add RAG citations for imaging findings: Each radiological finding should reference source (e.g., 'Kerley B lines indicate interstitial edema (Talley & O'Connor p.142, confidence 0.85)')

Create AMC-specific imaging scenarios: '68F post-op day 3 hip replacement, sudden SOB. CXR shows [specific findings]. Q1: Systematic CXR interpretation (ABCDE). Q2: Most likely diagnosis. Q3: Immediate management (3 steps).'

agent_evaluations.reviewer_notes: CRITICAL SCOPE ISSUE: This is a metadata inventory file (52 OSCE topics) with placeholder image paths, NOT individual radiology interpretation content. violations.issue: No specific medications or dosing protocols provided in OSCE content - only generic topic 'Hypocalcemia' without treatment details
violations.suggested_fix: Add acute hypocalcemia management protocol: calcium gluconate 10% 10-20mL IV over 10 minutes, then check corrected calcium, magnesium, PTH, vitamin D. Include chronic management with calcium carbonate 600mg BD-TDS PO + colecalciferol 1000 units daily

violations.issue: Missing PBS-compliant treatment recommendations for hypocalcemia management
violations.suggested_fix: Specify PBS-listed calcium supplements (calcium carbonate PBS code 1756T) and vitamin D (colecalciferol 1000 units PBS code 10183K)

violations.issue: No emergency vs chronic hypocalcemia treatment differentiation
violations.suggested_fix: Distinguish acute symptomatic hypocalcemia (IV calcium gluconate 10% 10-20mL over 10 min, can repeat) from chronic management (oral calcium + vitamin D)

violations.issue: Missing critical drug interaction warnings for calcium supplementation
violations.suggested_fix: Note: calcium reduces absorption of bisphosphonates (separate by 2h), levothyroxine (separate by 4h), ciprofloxacin (separate by 2h). Avoid calcium IV with digoxin (arrhythmia risk)

suggestions: Add specific medication protocols: Acute hypocalcemia - calcium gluconate 10% 10-20mL IV over 10 minutes (repeat if tetany persists), monitor ECG for QT interval normalization
Include magnesium correction protocol: magnesium sulphate 5g (20mmol) IV over 4 hours if Mg <0.5 mmol/L (hypocalcemia won't correct without correcting hypomagnesemia)
Specify chronic oral supplementation: calcium carbonate 600mg elemental calcium BD-TDS PO (take with food for better absorption) + colecalciferol 1000-2000 units daily
Add investigation pathway: check corrected calcium (adjust for albumin), ionized calcium, magnesium, phosphate, PTH, vitamin D (25-OH), renal function
Include Australian-specific dosing for severe symptomatic hypocalcemia: calcium gluconate 10% 10mL IV bolus, then infusion 10-20mL in 100mL dextrose 5% over 4-6 hours
Note PBS restrictions: Calcium + vitamin D combinations (e.g., Caltrate D) are PBS-listed for osteoporosis prevention (requires bone density scan documentation for authority)
strengths: Topic selection is clinically relevant (hypocalcemia is common electrolyte disorder requiring medication management)
8-minute time limit appropriate for assessment and management discussion
Gastroenterology specialty assignment correct (malabsorption, post-gastrectomy, pancreatitis can cause hypocalcemia)
References include appropriate Australian sources (John Murtagh General Practice, AMC Handbook)
agent_evaluations.detailed_feedback: This OSCE template for hypocalcemia lacks critical medication management content. While the topic is appropriate and references are Australian, there are NO specific medications, dosing protocols, or PBS compliance information provided. For a medication management evaluation, this is insufficient. The OSCE needs: (1) Acute treatment protocol - calcium gluconate 10% IV dosing, (2) Chronic management - oral calcium carbonate + colecalciferol with PBS codes, (3) Magnesium replacement protocol (essential - hypocalcemia won't correct without correcting hypomagnesemia), (4) Drug interactions (calcium with levothyroxine, bisphosphonates, antibiotics), (5) Monitoring parameters (corrected calcium target 2.10-2.55 mmol/L). Current format is a scenario shell without pharmacotherapy detail. Recommend adding comprehensive medication protocols following eTG/AMH guidelines before clinical deployment.
